title: Holding the zero-implementation boundary — audit-once-and-codify vs a standing fail-closed classifier
summary: Grounds decision #1770 (the end-state constellation-placement audit gate). The ratified rule is absolute — WE holds zero implementation, contract/protocol/interface only, never delivery runtime 'not even as a reference implementation' (platform-decisions.md constellation-placement rule 1, #1246/#1282). #1770 asked a binary question — is the line tight (A) or are there residuals (B)? — which is not a decidable fork at all: which branch obtains is a fact about the tree, settled by counting. The real question is one level up: what INSTRUMENT confirms the rule, and what keeps that confirmation true a month later? Two candidates: a codified end-state placement map written into the statute anchor, or a standing fail-closed path classifier run by check:standards on every build. The repo supplies its own decisive evidence. First, no enforcement exists today: grepping scripts/, .githooks/ and .github/workflows/ for the rule's lineage returns two prose comments and no check, so the '#1282: no NEW WE-resident delivery runtime may be added' clause is held by model judgment alone; the nearest guard (guard-backward-edge.mjs) is scoped to src/** and misses the ten blocks/ files that already import @frontierui. Second, the doc branch has already failed here: #1770's own lineage records a hand inventory on 2026-06-24 that explicitly CLEARED the gen-wrapper fixture, and eight weeks later scripts/gen-wrapper/genWrapper.mjs stands at 228 lines against frontierui/tools/gen-wrapper/genWrapper.mjs's 417 (263 diff lines, the whole #1518 live-mount variant system absent). Sharper still, that fixture was sanctioned as a 'reference fixture' by #892 on 2026-06-18 and #1282 withdrew the reference-implementation tier wholesale two days later on 2026-06-20 — it survived its own repeal, because a ruling changes a rule but enumerates nothing. Third, the status trigger is unsound: epic #1245's four filed children are all resolved while its declared first, load-bearing delete (blocks/router/, 2,843 tracked lines including a 619-line custom element) is untouched, so 'all blockedBy resolved' goes green over work never done. Measured residue: ~8,960 tracked non-test .ts lines under blocks/ (≈6,600 delivery runtime), plus capabilities/ (2,418), validation-generation/ (1,570, header self-declares 'the impl half'), guard/ (397), and the provider/registry pairs that are rule 2's literal example; against 92 same-path WE↔FUI file pairs of which 62 have drifted with no reconciliation gate in either repo. Prior-art survey: the boundary-enforcement tool family (dependency-cruiser, eslint-plugin-boundaries, import/no-restricted-paths, @nx/enforce-module-boundaries, Sheriff, Bazel visibility/package_group, ArchUnit and its ports, Java JPMS, Go internal packages, Python import-linter) converged independently on continuous, tagged, allow-list classification rather than periodic review; the architectural fitness-function literature (Ford/Parsons/Kua, Building Evolutionary Architectures) frames conformance as an ongoing measurement rather than a one-off judgment, with triggered pipeline gates the standard carrier for structural rules; the ADR and architecture-drift literature documents the decay of point-in-time records asked to do a living artifact's job, where stale documentation is worse than none because it manufactures false confidence; and standards bodies solve the same problem structurally — web-platform-tests keeps conformance artifacts in a repo that holds no implementation while each browser implements elsewhere, and OpenFeature splits its spec repo from every SDK. In-repo precedent exists but does NOT license the obvious answer: #2006 ruled the WE-website a mis-homed product under the same rule 1 and #2052 shipped its carrier, the fail-closed classifySurfacePaths in scripts/check-standards-rules.mjs where a zone path matching neither surface set is a hard error — yet that file's own comment records the whole-tree widening as considered and rejected, because classifying every tracked path 'would be noise and would red-gate the whole repo'. Drafting and then RUNNING the widened classifier confirms it: over all 6,980 tracked paths it yields 712 site / 1,114 standard / 124 impl / 4,256 neutral and 774 hard errors, including the contracts/, conformance-vectors/, capability-manifest/ and webcases/ directories the same inventory certifies as correctly placed, plus all twelve contract and types modules under blocks/; and it is GREEN on both motivating defects, because a path classifier cannot see file content or the sibling repo and the gen-wrapper divergence is FUI growing while WE stands still. The deeper correction is that the tempting inference — prose rots, code stays true — is false here. The repo contains two machine checks that have already rotted into no-ops: validatePlugWeFuiDrift, a real cross-repo byte-identity gate with PLUG_DRIFT_ENFORCED = true, went vacuous when #1047 deleted its subject plugs/ directory; and the #964 codegen-placement invariant went dead when #1730 deleted its subject module. Both are existsSync-guarded, so both report success while covering nothing. With the fixture that outlived its repeal and #1245's four filed slices covering four of sixteen named targets, that is four instances of ONE failure mode — silent scope-loss, an instrument that stops covering anything with nothing reporting the drop. So the survey's conclusion inverts the intuitive one: not a broader classifier but a NARROW, coverage-reporting instrument — re-point the dormant byte-parity gate at the declared WE↔FUI duplicate pair list (the only mechanism that catches the observed drift), add a new-path check over the named debt roots with a path-SET ratchet rather than line budgets, and make any guarded check whose subject has vanished ERROR rather than skip. Full grounding in reports/2026-08-17-zero-impl-boundary-enforcement.md.
